WHY MINDSCAPE

Intelligence is more than an answer.

A prediction tells us what a system produced.

We want to understand what it represented, which actions it took and how the outcome can be evaluated.

Mindscape develops AI research systems around those questions—investigating structured reasoning, cognitive representations, neural generalization and verifiable execution.

Explore the architecture →

Four directions. One ambition.

01 — Cognitive Architecture

Investigating how neural systems represent states, relationships, events and actions.

02 — Applied Reasoning & Verified Intelligence

Building systems such as Epitome that combine neural capabilities with structured scientific computation.

03 — Grounded & Multimodal Intelligence

Exploring representations of physical interactions, environments and multimodal observations.

04 — Evaluation & Reliability

Testing capabilities through controlled experiments, independent checks and reproducible evidence.

A little more
about Mindscape.

What is Mindscape, in simple terms?

Imagine teaching someone a board game. You explain the pieces, how they relate, the current position, and the moves allowed. Then you give examples and let them practise. Mindscape explores that idea for AI: provide the structure of a task, learn patterns from examples, and test the actions it takes.

Does it learn differently from other AI?

LLMs learn statistical patterns from large amounts of data, and those patterns can include useful representations of concepts. Mindscape puts an explicit structure around learning: entities, relationships, states, and allowed actions. It combines this structure with learned patterns, memory, and checks. Its coding system currently uses an LLM, so it is a different system design rather than a demonstrated replacement for LLMs. We are testing whether this approach can need fewer examples and produce more reliable results.

What has it been tested on?

The research includes software repair, numerical learning and physical dynamics. The separate Epitome applied system scored 36/36 on a targeted STEM hard set and 12/12 on a release holdout. These results measure bounded solver capabilities, not general reasoning or syllabus mastery. See the results and their limits.

Can I use or contribute to Mindscape?

Mindscape is an experimental research project. You can explore the source and reports, or get in touch about collaboration, research support, and ideas.
